trend: Strong continuation trend with high-volume MACD-confirmed EMA crossover; RSI approaching overbought but momentum intact
thesis: Hindustan Zinc is a high-conviction metals pick with a 38% net margin and 71.7% revenue growth, driven by rising LME zinc prices and silver volume growth acting as a dual earnings lever. The 2.6x volume surge on the technical breakout signals strong institutional re-entry, and Fwd PE of 13.5x remains inexpensive relative to the quality of cash flows and a historically generous dividend yield. Global zinc supply deficits and India's infrastructure-led galvanized steel demand provide a durable macro tailwind through FY26.
risk: A reversal in LME zinc prices due to China demand disappointment or a global risk-off trade could rapidly compress earnings given the commodity-linked revenue model. RSI at 62.84 suggests the stock is entering overbought territory — late entries above 540 may face short-term consolidation before the next leg up.

trend: Moderate recovery from 52-week low zone with EMA crossover and elevated volume; stock still ~17% below 52-week high

The 1.9x volume confirmation on the EMA crossover suggests smart money accumulation ahead of the Q2 results season which could show margin recovery from GTF engine grounding impacts. Fwd PE of 22x is reasonable for the only scaled, profitable LCC in one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets.

Revenue growth of only 6.2% reflects capacity constraints from grounded aircraft — a prolonged Pratt & Whitney engine resolution delay could cap upside.

trend: Strong continuation trend with full triple-indicator confluence; stock stabilising after RBI regulatory-overhang correction
thesis: Kotak Mahindra Bank is recovering strongly from its post-RBI digital banking restriction lows with a confirmed trend continuation, and 21% revenue growth alongside 28.47% net margin reflects the franchise's superior credit quality and cost efficiency vs. private banking peers. With Fwd PE of 15.8x and beta of only 0.27, this is a low-volatility compounder where the RBI overhang is progressively lifting as digital onboarding normalises. DII flows into quality private banks ahead of potential RBI rate cuts make this a high-probability near-term swing.

The hypergrowth revenue number (208%) is partly base-effect driven and likely to normalise significantly in coming quarters, which could disappoint momentum investors.
